prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Conservative Party Manifesto 2010 – Summary (≤500 words)

Core vision and values
- “Big Society, not big government”: empower citizens, families, communities and frontline professionals; devolve power; transparency and accountability; responsibility in public finances; enterprise and aspiration; “we’re all in this together.”

Economy and public finances
- Urgent deficit reduction: Emergency Budget; Office for Budget Responsibility; £6bn in-year waste cuts; freeze most public sector pay for one year (protecting the lowest paid); review raising state pension age; cut Child Trust Funds/tax credits for higher earners; cap very high public pensions; reduce MPs by 10%, Ministers’ pay cut/freeze.
- Stop Labour’s “jobs tax”: raise NI thresholds to spare most workers and employers.
- Growth model shift to saving, investment, exports and hi-tech/green industries; implement Dyson proposals; refocus R&D credits; improve trade support.
- Encourage saving: restore earnings link for basic state pension; auto-enrolment; end near-obligation to buy annuity at 75; raise inheritance tax threshold to £1m via non-dom levy.
- Consumer debt: create Consumer Protection Agency; clearer credit rules; free national financial advice (levy-funded).
- Jobs and welfare: single Work Programme; reassess Incapacity Benefit; tougher conditionality and community work for long-term claimants; NI holiday for new firms’ first 10 hires; 400,000 apprenticeships/training; SME procurement target 25%.
- Taxes/regulation: cut corporation tax to 25% and small companies’ rate to 20%, funded by simplifying reliefs; Office of Tax Simplification; regulatory budgets; faster business start-up; open procurement.
- Immigration: annual cap on non‑EU economic migrants; default transitional controls for new EU members; tighter student visas; English test for spouses.

Regional growth and infrastructure
- High Speed Rail (London–Midlands–North), oppose new runways at Heathrow/Stansted/Gatwick; rail franchise reform; superfast broadband via infrastructure access (possible licence fee use); local enterprise partnerships; allow councils to retain uplift in business rates.

Public services, banking and green economy
- Public service reform: payment by results; mutuals/co-ops; publish spending over £25k and senior pay.
- Banking: Bank of England regains prudential supervision; bank levy; boost competition; expand SME credit.
- Green economy: Green Investment Bank; carbon price floor; shift tax mix toward environmental taxes.

Big Society, families, health and education
- Big Society Bank (unclaimed assets); community organisers; neighbourhood grants; National Citizen Service; refocus Lottery to core causes.
- Families: recognise marriage/civil partnerships in tax; end couple penalty in tax credits; two-year council tax freeze; extend flexible working and shared parental leave; protect childhood (marketing curbs); keep and refocus Sure Start; 4,200 more health visitors; stable relationship support.
- NHS: real-terms funding rises; patient choice of any qualified provider; GP commissioning; scrap non-clinical targets; independent NHS Board; publish outcomes; 24/7 urgent care access; Cancer Drugs Fund; personal health/social care budgets; voluntary social care insurance; stronger public health with “health premium.”
- Schools: raise teacher quality and discipline; phonics and age-6 reading test; more rigorous curriculum/exams; technical academies; expand academies/free schools; pupil premium; protect special schools.

Crime, policing, civil liberties and localism
- Crime: tougher knife sentences; alcohol licensing crackdown; elected police commissioners; cut police paperwork; monthly local crime data; Border Police Force; honest sentencing; payment-by-results rehabilitation; abstinence-based drug orders.
- Politics and the state: recall for MPs; donation cap; curb lobbying; fewer MPs/special advisers; open data rights; quango cull; local referendums and veto on high council tax; community right to buy/run services; open, incentive-based planning; first-time buyer stamp duty threshold to £250k; social housing mobility; scrap ID cards and ContactPoint; reform DNA retention; UK Bill of Rights (replace HRA); review vetting; free vote on Hunting Act repeal.

Environment
- 80% emissions cut by 2050; smart grid/meters; emissions performance standard; new nuclear (no subsidy); four CCS plants; offshore grid; Green Deal for home efficiency; protect habitats/green belts; fisheries reform; tree planting; bTB badger control; honest food labelling; supermarket ombudsman; zero-waste drive.

Foreign policy, defence and aid
- National Security Council; Strategic Defence and Security Review; support Afghanistan mission; renew Trident; procurement reform; restore Military Covenant (e.g., double operational allowance, family support).
- Europe: referendum lock on future EU power transfers; Sovereignty Bill; repatriate powers on key areas; never join Euro.
- International development: 0.7% GNI by 2013 in law; transparency and results; focus on poorest; at least £500m/year on malaria; pro‑development trade; stabilisation and reconstruction capability.
